children: The sample was collected from The Lalit in New Delhi and found non-compliant in laboratory analysis, while Nestle said its product is safe and meets regulatory requirements

A sample of Nestle India’s Low Fat Dairy Whitener collected from The Lalit hotel in New Delhi has been found non-compliant with food safety standards following laboratory testing conducted under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), according to a regulatory notice.

The sample was collected from the premises of M/s Bharat Hotels, which operates The Lalit in Connaught Place. A Food Analyst’s laboratory subsequently examined the product and determined that the sample did not meet requirements under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

FSSAI communicated the laboratory findings to the food business operator and provided a copy of the analysis report. The regulator subsequently issued a notice to Bharat Hotels Ltd. concerning the Nestle product identified in the test.
Sale Of Product Ordered To Stop

As part of the regulatory action, the food business operator was directed to immediately prohibit the sale of the identified product. The operator was also given an opportunity to appeal against the Food Analyst’s findings within the prescribed period under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

The notice relates to the specific sample collected from the hotel premises and the laboratory findings recorded against it. The regulatory process allows the concerned food business operator to contest the analysis within the stipulated timeframe.

Nestle India, however, said its Low Fat Dairy Whitener is safe for consumption and meets applicable regulatory requirements.The company said phosphorus is naturally present in milk and therefore also occurs in products made using milk-based ingredients. Nestle said FSSAI laboratory reports measure total phosphorus against the applicable additive limit but do not account separately for phosphorus that occurs naturally in milk-based ingredients.

According to Nestle, its product meets the prescribed limits for added phosphorus under the Food Safety and Standards Regulations, including on an as-consumed basis. The company said it has been engaging with the authorities through the prescribed process and has submitted data on comparable milk-based products to demonstrate the presence of naturally occurring phosphorus.
